images.prompt: Edit this Yiling burning camp film still into LATE EVENING JUST AFTER SUNSET, with convincing live-action NIGHTFALL lighting, full-frame 16:9. Keep the exact camera, enormous valley encampment, road bend, foreground cart, left forked bare tree, right watchtower and mountain notch. The sun has completely set below the horizon. Sky is dark indigo charcoal with only a very thin residual dim dusk band behind the distant ridge, no bright gray daytime sky and no sunlight. Dominant illumination is the large vigorous fires: localized flickering amber and orange light lights the facing tent fabric, rough wood and dry dirt road, shadows fall away naturally. Faint cool skylight supplies just enough detail in unlit regions so textures are visible. The light should physically come from fires, not a global orange overlay or a simple underexposure filter. Large fires remain vivid and fierce, multiple distinct smoke plumes rise and are backlit at lower edges but dark above. Preserve huge scale and readable foreground/midground material, authentic coarse canvas, strained rope, broken cart and dry scorched earth. Tents at different stages of burning with believable structural damage, not plastic spotless tents. Deep focus, strong natural tonal separation, photographic realism, dark nightfall atmosphere with clear narrative readability. No people added, no rain, no wet soil, no puddles, no fog veil, no extreme blue-orange grading, no captions or text. This is the evening stage of a sequence that will progress later into night and finally predawn; do not show dawn or sunrise here.

Create a single full-frame 16:9 photorealistic historical live-action film reference still, an EDIT/REDESIGN of reference 1 for the same Yiling retreat road. Reference 1 defines geography and wooden supply cart, NOT clean costumes. Reference 2 defines the burning camp and motivated night lighting. It is now DEEP NIGHT, hours after sunset, near-black charcoal sky with dark smoke and NO sunset pink, NO daylight, NO dawn. Fire from actual burning tents is the main illumination on actors, complemented by faint neutral cool night fill for readable faces/hands/feet. Do NOT merely darken a daytime image.
Medium-wide full-body view of TWO weary retreating ordinary soldiers pulling and pushing the SAME simple wooden two-wheel supply cart toward camera and slightly left. Keep both men, cart and feet entirely in frame with breathing room, people each about 35 percent of frame height maximum, so surroundings remain important. Background a few other small scattered retreating soldiers and the vast camp still burning; not an orderly march. CRUCIAL COSTUME REDESIGN: these men have struggled through fire and defeat. Front soldier with disheveled partially loosened hair knot, NO tall neat hat, coarse faded gray-brown tunic with open rumpled collar, uneven frayed sleeves, one torn lower hem, irregular soot and sweat streaks on natural skin, one battered lamellar shoulder panel hanging a little loose but secured; no complete pristine uniform. Rear man visibly different: crooked worn cloth head wrap with loose end, dusty patched brown tunic, torn cuff, one forearm wrapped in a dirty cloth strip, scuffed irregular leather armor straps and slack worn waist sash. Leg wraps disordered but not dragging around ankles; shoes still practical. Damage localized where singed and rubbed, not everyone uniformly a rag costume. No shiny symmetrical new armor, no matching clean costumes, no ceremonial headwear, no perfect waist belts. Express exhaustion and focused urgency with hunched effort, closed mouths and normal believable anatomy. Hands firmly grip separate cart handles or rear rail, correct real load bearing, cart cargo tied in worn fabric sacks. Dry ash, broken tent poles, shredded canvas and scattered pottery beside the clear road. Real detailed textiles, fractured wood grain, face pores and sweat, documentary war-film realism. Large nearby flames still burn and light faces directionally; shadows readable, no flat global amber cast. No rain, puddles, wet soil, uniform fog, blood or gore, logos, captions, lettering, CG appearance or blur.

Edit reference image 1 into the SAME camera composition but HOURS BEFORE DAWN, after a long night of fire and retreat. Full-frame 16:9 photorealistic historical film still. Reference 1 is the exact geography, wide lateral view, scale and road, NOT its tidy clothes or sunset illumination. Reference 2 defines the disheveled worn soldiers and damaged cart cargo. Keep every soldier SMALL at the scale of reference 1, full body, the group and one cart moving RIGHT TO LEFT along road in lower third. Front pulling man has loose messy hair knot, torn gray-brown tunic, loosened battered asymmetrical lamellar shoulder piece; rear pushing man has crooked dirty cloth headwrap, tattered brown tunic and worn straps, matching reference 2 at distance. Remaining men vary in localized singed hems, rumpled collars, soot, dusty irregular wraps and sagging kit. No tall formal hats, no neat uniforms or parade ranks. Exhausted upright walking, subdued hunched posture, hands attached to shafts and rear cart rail, no gore. Do not enlarge or pose characters.
CRUCIAL TIME OF NIGHT: remove ALL warm sunset pink from the sky. Upper sky deep charcoal blue-black; distant horizon only a very faint cold slate glow of approaching predawn, no visible sun, no pink sunrise, no daylight. Mountain and watchtower silhouettes read against dark sky. Main light comes from ongoing orange fires within camp, illuminating smoke bases and the side of retreating figures facing fire; a faint neutral cool ambient fill keeps road and ragged fabric readable without looking like day. Large substantial fires still occupy several distant terrace bands, while many nearer tents are now more collapsed and charred after hours of destruction. Not an extinguished quiet empty camp: fire and smoke remain powerful. Road is DRY DUSTY EARTH with ash, never wet, no rain or puddles. Preserve cart path, left dead tree, right watchtower and upper-center ridge notch; enormous camp scale and real coarse fabric/wood detail. Camera stays on side of road wide and low enough for credible scale, not aerial. No fog blanket, no glow wash, no CGI miniature, no captions, text or borders.
